title: fix: skip unchanged disclosure and shell state writes during resize
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closed Review/file disclosures briefly reveal and re-hide on equal reactive invalidations during resize. Broad shell refreshes also reassign two unchanged standalone `inert` bindings. These writes create unnecessary style work.

## User Impact

The UI keeps the same layout, live resizing and disclosure behavior with fewer style passes. This is a work-count improvement, not a claimed frame-latency or smooth-resize improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compare the disclosure owner's existing applied open/active/instant fields instead of the newly allocated object's identity. Add equality-filtered boolean memos for the two standalone shell bindings. No scheduler/transaction changes, new dependencies, or runtime size-cap adjustments.

## Evidence

Acceptance was set before running: a p95 **or style/layout passes per input** improvement beyond A/A, with frame medians preserved. The style-count route qualifies: sidebar styles −23.37% Chromium / −21.65% WebKit, split −11.38% / −12.27%, beyond A/A. Layout variations remain within A/A or improve. Every paired frame median is unchanged or improved, but no meaningful p95 win is claimed.

Warm synthetic production UI: 2,000 messages, split panes, 20 Review files; desktop 1440×1000, default CPU. Requested input cadence 60 Hz; viewport commands serialize and actual delivery is slower. rAF intervals are browser-local callback gaps, not display presentation timestamps. WebKit native Timeline reports application elapsed work; Firefox has no native style/layout trace through this harness. Traced frame timings do not enter acceptance. Native counts and untraced timing each have 20 rotated base/head/base-control pairs. Fractions are medians of per-gesture fractions; paired deltas are medians of pairwise deltas, so they need not equal ratios of the displayed medians. Host load and actual event rates are retained in measurements.csv. No 4×/mobile remeasurement in this bounded round.

Firefox window p95 paired +0.66% versus +8.56% A/A. Absolute medians of p95 values shift with host load; paired comparisons retain run order. Firefox has no native style/layout count in this harness. WebKit measurements are application time. All handles ended exactly +35 px. No ResizeObserver loop errors.

</details>

Production LOC 760 → 768; tests 70 → 104. Two memos added; no new effects, listeners, queries, flushes or owner APIs. The existing opacity snapshot lint warning is unchanged. `ci:full` covers shell/shared-UI scope. Remaining resize work and historical 4×/mobile cells are outside this focused PR.

The attached before/after split-resize captures are synthetic-only and byte-identical (same final geometry and appearance).

CI repair: the first run (`42435906075`) passed every UI, Control UI E2E, browser-extension, real-Gateway, type/lint, and performance job; its test-line ratchet rejected the 34 newly added regression lines. A focused follow-up allocates exactly those 34 lines and merges current main (`e64215c411f1addeeb765568c5d82e6a99f9652d`) without changing the measured runtime patch. This regression detects 40 redundant hidden mutations on base for each disclosure variant, so it protects the actual waste removed here.

Current-main local attribution: at `e64215c411f1addeeb765568c5d82e6a99f9652d`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 5e1a27a9bcc4ed52cecd2420409b8c0331ddf4be --no-merge-base` fails at 6,571,194 test lines versus a 6,571,129 ceiling (65 over). The repaired candidate has 6,571,228 lines versus a 6,571,163 ceiling (the same 65 over). The latest completed scheduled main run predates this base, so its passing ratchet is not evidence for the newer tree. No unrelated debt is added to this PR's allocation.

Replacement run `42437191863` (attempt 1, head `f071c393851f4be9e334287d3bae417ef2f32d3d`) is complete: every UI, E2E, browser-extension, real-Gateway, type/lint and performance job passed. Only `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and its aggregate failed, with the same 65-line overage reproduced at the actual merge base. Native replacement-head recovery uses this recorded baseline-failure exception; CI is not described as green.
